title: observability: enhance token+KV cost & latency dashboard and alert tuning for batch workloads
author: Priya Shah
description:
Motivation: Customers run mixed workloads (sync low-latency chat + async batch) on the same model variants. Existing dashboards surface overall token cost and p95 latency but do not attribute cost/latency between KV-cache hits/misses or between sync vs async routes. This makes it hard to tune batching, caching policies, and alert thresholds for bursty batch workloads.

What I changed: single PR that adds enhanced token-level and KV-cache observability, dashboard panels, and tuned alerting rules: 1) emit new metrics from the serving runtime: redwood.kv_cache.hit_rate, redwood.kv_cache.miss_rate, redwood.token.latency_breakdown (sync/async), redwood.token.cost_per_1k_by_route; 2) add dashboard JSON with new panels for token cost breakdown by route/model, KV hit/miss heatmap, latency CDFs (p50/p90/p95/p99) split by KV hit/miss, and a dedicated view for batch job performance; 3) introduce adaptive alert rules that use different thresholds for Dedicated vs Hosted customers and that suppress alerts during autoscaling/burst windows; 4) update docs + runbook with investigation steps and tuning guidance for batching and quantization tradeoffs.

Checklist: - [x] runtime metric emission (instrumented in metrics collector) - [x] dashboard panels + templating (model, route, deployment_tier) - [x] alert rules with suppression windows and burn-rate guardrails - [x] unit + integration tests for new metric tags and dashboard validator - [x] docs & runbook updates

Notes: CI showed a flaky integration test on the first run (kv-metrics-collector::test_cache_counters). I addressed a race in the test by adding a short backoff and made the metric emission idempotent for startup. Dashboard JSON validated locally using our dashboard linter. This PR is primarily observability (no user-facing API changes) but is high-impact for oncall and platform reliability teams.

release_notes: Enhancement: token-level and KV-cache observability panels + tuned alerting. Adds new metrics: redwood.kv_cache.hit_rate, redwood.kv_cache.miss_rate, redwood.token.latency_breakdown, redwood.token.cost_per_1k_by_route. Includes runbook for investigating token cost regressions and guidance for batching/quantization tradeoffs.
notes_for_oncall: New alerts introduce suppression during autoscale and burn-rate checks - if you see repeated alerts, verify suppression windows and autoscale events.
Use dashboard templating to filter by model/route/tier. Check kv_cache.hit_rate before escalating token latency alerts.
